contradictions.detail: The listing says every service was done in a Porsche Center. The Carfax shows 2026 work at German Import Garage (Truckee) and Reno Rennsport (Sparks), which are independents.
The listing says Rainforest Green Metallic; the Carfax records Oxford green. Photos show a dark green metallic. This is likely a naming difference, but check the paint code on the option sticker.

critical_evidence.evidence: There is no IMS retrofit or Solution invoice. The 02/2003 flywheel job with the transmission out (45,686 mi) predates aftermarket retrofits, and the Carfax summary does not mention the IMS. The door-jamb build month is not examined here, so dual-row vs single-row cannot be established for a 2000 model-year car.
Carfax shows an oil and filter change at Reno Rennsport on 05/28/2026 at 128,733 mi. There is no filter-cut photo and no oil analysis showing debris or glycol results.
No borescope images or PPI report provided.
No cold-start video captured or offered.

No certificate provided. Carfax records 'emissions passed 05/2026' (jurisdiction unstated) and a dealer emissions inspection on 09/29/2026. That is supportive but not a CA certificate within the 90-day window.

documentation.rationale: Identity and terms are strong: VIN decode matches, the price is itemised, and the Carfax shows owners, title, mileage trail and 31 service records. The maintenance half is incomplete. There are no itemised invoices and no record of IMS, water pump, AOS or cooling work. The 2010 damage event has no detail or repair documentation.

condition.rationale: Observed in the photos: heavily creased and cracked seat leather on both front seats, and steering-wheel wear. Paint and soft top look presentable at photo resolution. Mechanical condition is unproven apart from a recent oil service and an emissions pass. The 2010 damage is unexplained, and there is no underside evidence for a car kept in Truckee for 17 years.

price_value.rationale: Asking $34,989 against a fair-value estimate of $18,383-$23,718 (mid $21,109). That is roughly 65% over mid. Comparable high-mile cabriolets sold at $14,000-$22,000. The price also carries an undocumented IMS, unexplained damage and likely deferred M96 catch-up.

mission_fit.rationale: It meets the manual requirement and has a strong point of view for Highway 1. However, the asking price sits above the $27,000 ceiling, and M96 engine risk without IMS evidence works against the reliable, low-risk, easy-to-resell bridge brief.

logistics.rationale: Reno is roughly a day's drive from Carmel. A franchised Porsche dealer with independent Porsche specialists nearby makes a PPI before payment realistic. The car has a long CA registration history and passed emissions in 2026.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: A 6-speed manual in an attractive dark green over Savanna, with factory Turbo Look I wheels. Offsetting this, it is a Cabriolet (the less desirable body) with worn leather.

seller_questions: Can you send a photo of the driver's door-jamb sticker showing the production month and paint code?
Do you have the itemised invoices behind the Carfax records, and has the IMS bearing ever been retrofitted? If so, which part and which shop?
What did the 05/10/2010 damage report involve, which panels were affected, and are there repair invoices or paint-meter readings?
When were the water pump, thermostat, expansion tank and front radiators last replaced? Please include mileage and invoices.
Did the 02/2003 flywheel job include a clutch and an updated rear main seal? Is there an invoice?
What did your 09/29/2026 safety/brake/emissions inspection find? Can we see the full multipoint sheet?
Can you provide a CA smog certificate, or allow a California-equivalent smog check before purchase?
Will you allow an independent PPI with borescope, coolant pressure test and a Durametric/PIWIS cam-deviation scan before any deposit?
Can you shoot an uninterrupted cold-start video from fully cold, including the exhaust tips for the first two minutes?
What are the DOT date codes on all four tires?
Has the air-oil separator been replaced? Any smoke at startup?
Is the factory hardtop included, and does the soft top cycle cleanly with no hydraulic leaks?
ppi_focus: Borescope all six cylinders, with attention to bore scoring on 4-6.
Coolant pressure test, expansion-tank seams, and an oil sample for glycol and metals; cut the oil filter.
Durametric/PIWIS scan for stored codes and cam deviation values (Variocam and chain wear).
Clutch engagement point, DMF chatter, and an RMS weep at the engine/transaxle junction.
Paint meter and structural check around the 2010 damage area; inspect front crossmember and radiator supports.
Underside corrosion check given Truckee winters: subframes, suspension arms, brake lines, exhaust.
Front bumper off or inspection of radiators and condensers for debris and corrosion.
Soft-top operation, hydraulic rams and lines, rear window, and water ingress in the footwells.
AOS symptoms: crankcase vacuum at the oil filler cap, smoke on cold start.
Coil packs and plug tubes for cracks or oil fouling; tire date codes.
what_would_change_verdict: A price move toward the fair-value range (about $18k-$24k) would change the value picture substantially.
An invoice showing an LN IMS retrofit or Solution, or a replacement engine, plus invoices for cooling and AOS work, would lift documentation and condition.
A clean independent PPI with good borescope results, no glycol in the oil, healthy cam deviation and a dry underside would raise condition.
Repair documentation showing the 2010 damage was minor and properly fixed would clear the accident flag.
Bore scoring, coolant in the oil, structural repair evidence or heavy underside corrosion would move it sharply down.
evidence.mission_note: It satisfies the manual, point-of-view part of the enthusiast-bridge brief, but the asking price is above the $27,000 ceiling. The M96 3.4 with no IMS evidence is the opposite of the low-risk, easy-resale bridge the accelerated_bridge mode calls for.
evidence.rationale: The listing and its Carfax establish identity firmly. The VIN decodes to a 2000 Carrera Cabriolet 3.4. There are two personal owners, no title brands, a coherent mileage trail to 128,912 mi, 31 service records, and a 6-speed manual visible in the photos. Observed against it: an unexplained damage report dated 05/10/2010 with no repair documentation, and heavily cracked front-seat leather in the photos. The dealer's 'every service at a Porsche Center' claim conflicts with independent-shop entries on the Carfax. The model's decisive engine evidence is entirely absent: no IMS invoice or build month, no oil analysis or filter inspection, no borescope, no cold-start video. Cooling-system and AOS history also do not appear in the report. The 2003 flywheel replacement is documented, but clutch and RMS status since then is not. Asking $34,989 sits about 65% above the $21,109 fair-value mid and above the $27,000 ceiling, before any M96 catch-up.
evidence.next_action: Email Porsche Reno asking for the door-jamb sticker photo, itemised invoices (IMS, cooling, AOS, 2003 clutch/RMS), details of the 2010 damage repair, and written agreement to an independent PPI with borescope before any deposit.
